statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk is 21%, inside the 20-24% watch band and below the 25% block threshold.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH rather than a block. The narrow danger window spans 12:00Z-15:00Z on 1 October, covering initial jobless claims at 12:30Z, the U.S. cash open at 13:30Z, the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI at 13:45Z and ISM Manufacturing at 14:00Z. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ edges to 30,838 near the overnight high on thin Golden Week volume while cash NDX closed at its session low; Tail holds at 21%
body: Observed state at the assessment cutoff: NQ Dec-26 futures last printed 30,838.00, plus 139.25 points or 0.45%, at 22:16 ET on roughly 31.0k Globex contracts, inside an overnight range of 30,684.50-30,845.75 and about 8 points below that high against a 30,698.75 previous close. NQ is therefore holding near the upper edge of its overnight range, which is a mild amplifier, but the whole Globex range spans only about 161 points, or 0.52%, on thin turnover. The cash session argues the other way: NASDAQ-100 closed 30 September at 30,408.50, plus 0.23%, which was the low of its 30,408.50-30,630.45 range after a late-session bout of volatility erased the full intraday gain. That completed fade is the most recent observed evidence on mean reversion, and it shows reversion still working. The tape was rotational rather than aligned: the S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,651.54 and the Dow fell 0.86% to 50,906.05 while the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.24% to 26,861.06. Cross-asset backdrop: VIX settled at 16.34, up 1.87%, within a 15.62-16.61 range and near the low end of its 13.38-35.30 annual range. The Federal Reserve H.15 release for 29 September shows the 2-year at 4.89%, the 10-year at 5.26% and the 30-year at 5.59%; market reporting for 30 September had the 30-year easing to about 5.553% and the 2-year down roughly four basis points after August core PCE printed at 3.0% year on year and 0.2% month on month, with headline at 3.4%, all lighter than expected. Odds of an October rate hike fell from about 51% to roughly 37%. WTI is near $90.04, down 0.42%, and Brent near $97.80, down 0.24%. Asia is firm but divergent: the Nikkei 225 trades at 68,346.84, plus 2.39%, led by AI and semiconductor names after Micron reported record fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $54.23B and guided fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue to $61.5B plus or minus $1.5B. Hong Kong and mainland China are closed for National Day, so regional liquidity is thinner than usual. Risk reading: the amplifiers that would justify crossing the 25% block threshold are not present together. NQ sits near its overnight high, which counts, and the Asian semiconductor bid is strong, but the Nikkei's 2.39% gain against NQ's 0.45% is a divergence rather than aligned one-way structure, the overnight range is narrow on thin Golden Week volume, VIX is near annual lows, yields are falling rather than rising, and the last completed cash session faded entirely from its high. No persistent directional efficiency, shallow-pullback sequence or failed-retracement pattern has been observed on NQ. Tail therefore holds at 21%, inside the watch band. Stress stays at 70% because the environment remains genuinely difficult: elevated absolute yields, oil near $90, a late-session reversal in the last cash session, and an event stack of jobless claims, the final manufacturing PMI and ISM Manufacturing today followed by September payrolls tomorrow. Confidence is 88% on a corroborated futures quote, a confirmed cash close, official H.15 yields, current oil and VIX levels, a live Asian session and a verified seven-day U.S. calendar. The shared Finviz context file was collected at 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with partial collection status, roughly 27 hours old and well outside the 90-minute freshness limit, so it was treated as stale and excluded from this assessment; independent research carried the full evidence load.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opens in the green EA_ON band with Tail 15-16% and Stress 65% through the Asian and European hours of 30 September, firms from 11:00Z as the U.S. session approached, and crosses into the yellow WATCH band at 12:00Z with Tail 20%. Tail peaked at 23% across 15:00Z-16:00Z with Stress at 72%, then eased through the U.S. afternoon and overnight to close the window at Tail 21%, Stress 70% and Confidence 88% at 01:00Z on 1 October. Dominant mode was mixed in every one of the 24 available hours, and Confidence held in an 85-88% band throughout.
outlookSummary: The published path keeps Tail inside the 20-24% watch band for all 24 forecast hours, so the mapped state stays WATCH and yellow throughout. Tail eases to the 20% floor through the quiet late-Asian hours while Hong Kong and mainland China are shut for National Day, firms to 21% around the European open, and builds to a conditional peak of 24% across 13:00Z-14:00Z where the U.S. cash open, the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI and ISM Manufacturing stack inside two hours. Stress tracks that shape from 69% up to 75% and back. Nothing beyond the current clock-hour is observed: every later hour states its structure conditionally, with the depth of the first retracement after the 12:30Z claims print and the behaviour of pullbacks after the cash open named as the decisive tells. The window closes with scores at the band floor and a pre-payroll overhang, since September employment data lands at 12:30Z on 2 October, outside this forecast window. Confidence decays from 88% to 85% purely with forecast distance.

forecastDetail.comment: NQ at 30,838.00 and plus 0.45% sits about 8 points under the 30,845.75 overnight high, but cash NDX closed at its session low of 30,408.50 after a full intraday fade, so reversion is still functioning and Tail holds at 21% in the watch band.

Hong Kong and mainland China are shut for National Day, thinning the regional bid; continued rotation inside the 30,684.50-30,845.75 overnight band would hold Tail at the 20% floor, while a break above that high which sustains would be the first genuine amplifier.

The quietest Globex stretch, with no scheduled release inside the hour; band-floor scores assume thin Golden Week turnover persists, and a liquidity-driven extension on that turnover would not by itself qualify as Tail evidence.

Tokyo moves toward its close as European futures wake up; the conditional tell is whether the Micron-driven semiconductor bid survives the Japanese cash close, with VIX at 16.34 near the low end of its 13.38-35.30 annual range offering no tail corroboration.

Tail firms a single point to 21% on the conditional expectation that European futures add volume and widen the overnight range; the depth of the first European pullback is the tell, with soft August core PCE at 3.0% year on year still a supportive backdrop.

The European cash open can deliver a directional impulse, which is why conditional Tail sits at 21%, but one clean leg is not Tail; repeated extension after a failed retracement would be the amplifier, and yields softened on 30 September with the 30-year near 5.553%.
